A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Retained material can be matched across section moves and renumbering.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C report original simulations and adversarial-attack experiments, including embedding perturbations and downstream classification results.

after.justification: Original empirical results remain and are updated, with additional experiments on deeper GINs, heterophilic datasets, and large graphs in Appendices C.6-C.8.

M1.justification: The original Prob-PGD objective and Algorithm 1 remain, but Appendix C.8 introduces a distinct scalable approximation, Prob. It samples candidate existing edges and greedily deletes the objective-maximizing edge at each iteration, substantially changing the search procedure and restricting attacks to deletions.

E1.justification: v4 retains the earlier datasets and adds Chameleon and Squirrel for heterophilic node classification, plus ogbn-arxiv, ogbn-mag, ogbn-products, and pokec for large-graph embedding attacks. This extends coverage to new graph populations, heterogeneous structure, and million-node environments.

E2.justification: Random and Wst-PGD remain the comparators in the existing experiments. Figure 5 adds a majority-class classifier reference, while Appendix C.8 evaluates a stochastic greedy version of the worst-case attack, Wst, alongside the new Prob approximation.

E3.justification: Appendix C.2 changes the reported node-classification learning rate from 0.001 to 0.01 and graph-classification hidden dimensions from 64 to {32,64}. Added experiments introduce deeper GIN configurations, H2GCN with specified heterophilic-data splits, and a 200-edge deletion protocol for large graphs. These are substantive reported setting changes and new evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: Appendix C.6 adds experiments varying the internal MLP depth of GIN to test applicability beyond the simplified convolutional architecture. Appendix C.8 adds computational scalability analysis with runtime and peak memory measurements. The earlier structural case study and five-layer depth/activation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v1 reports downstream averages over five attack repetitions without dispersion in Table 1. v4 reports averages over ten pretrained models with plus-minus values and explicitly reports means and standard deviations for the H2GCN experiments. The existing 200 random-weight trials remain; this is not simply a five-to-ten increase in the same repetition count.

E6.justification: Table 1 is extensively revised: for example, MUTAG GCN accuracy after Prob-PGD changes from 0.29 to 42.89 ± 4.86%. Revised settings and aggregation prevent treating this as a same-setting performance improvement. Figures 2 and 5 also change, and Tables 5-7 add substantial results, including Squirrel's larger embedding disruption without the greatest accuracy degradation.

T1.justification: Remark 2 changes the permutation-alignment criterion from the unscripted spectral norm to the Frobenius norm. The principal stability theorems, assumptions, structural proposition, and proof arguments remain substantively unchanged; added standard filter and architecture formulas mainly expand exposition.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: distribution-aware embedding stability, an exact graph-filter characterization, a multilayer bound, structural interpretation, and task-agnostic attacks. The additional experiments support these claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: v4 explicitly explains that maximizing embedding disruption need not maximize misclassification, using Squirrel as evidence. It also cautiously suggests extending the analysis to MPNNs and discusses the efficiency-versus-optimality tradeoff of restricted greedy search. Earlier structural and depth-related interpretations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 newly specifies losses, Adam optimization, weight decay, training epochs, the 250-iteration PGD limit, and approximately ten-minute Cora attack times. v4 also clarifies the simplified GIN implementation and supplies technical details for the added experiments. The code URL and stated V100 hardware were already present in v1.

R1.justification: v4 adds two Parada-Mayorga stability papers to related work and references supporting OGB datasets, H2GCN, and standard graph filters. The central positioning against worst-case stability analysis remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section structure remain largely intact. v4 locally rewrites experimental descriptions, expands implementation explanations, moves second-moment estimation from Appendix C.5 to C.3, and adds acknowledgments and revised author information. The new scientific sections do not constitute a wholesale language rewrite.

P2.justification: v4 adds the filter-reference Table 3 and experimental Tables 5-7; the earlier architecture table is retained as Table 4. Table 1 is redesigned for percentages and uncertainty, Figure 2 corrects the adjacency/Laplacian axis labels, and Figure 5 is redrawn with a majority-class reference. Existing appendix plots are consolidated and relocated.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially strengthens empirical assessment and reproducibility: central downstream results gain model-level variability reporting, training details become more explicit, and new experiments examine deeper architectures, heterophily, and computational feasibility beyond small graphs. The Squirrel discussion also qualifies the connection between embedding disruption and classification failure. These address important reporting and validation gaps in v1. The scalability evidence concerns the greedy approximation, however, and does not establish scalability of the original full PGD procedure.
